title: eml-parsing: add .eml support to MailPeek

close_reason: All 5 task groups closed. .eml parsing implemented via postal-mime (forceRfc822Attachments:true for non-inlined nested-message drill-down, matching .msg's innerMsgContent pattern), wired into parseEmailFile(), 8 new tests passing. Two things discovered during implementation and recorded in design.md/spec.md: postal-mime's node.subMessage is internal-only (not the public API the original plan assumed) and postal-mime is ESM-only requiring a dynamic import. title: Marketplace-listing polish: keywords, categories, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, README packaging fix
description: docs/plans/publish_to_marketplace.md Section 2. Added package.json keywords (email/msg/eml/outlook/viewer/mail/message/attachments) and a second category (Visualization, alongside Other). Created THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md at repo root covering all 9 bundled production dependencies (incl. transitive), with copyright lines and full license text appendices for the 4 distinct licenses involved (BSD-2-Clause, Apache-2.0, MIT, MIT-0) -- built from a direct license-checker scan, not assumed. Found and fixed a real bug while verifying the README-as-Marketplace-page item: vsce package requires a README.md next to extension/package.json, but none existed there (only the repo-root README.md) -- the packaged .vsix had zero listing content. Fixed by having the package script copy ../README.md to extension/README.md (via a portable node -e one-liner, not a symlink, for Windows contributor safety) before vsce package; extension/README.md is gitignored as a generated artifact. Also directly verified vsce's relative-link rewriting (using the repository field) actually works: docs/plans/*.md links in the bundled README got rewritten to https://github.com/saradindusengupta/mailpeek/blob/HEAD/... automatically -- confirmed by diffing the packaged copy, not assumed from vsce's docs.
close_reason: Verified via npm run compile/test/lint/license-check (all green, 22/22 tests) and two full npm run package runs -- confirmed the packaged .vsix now includes extension/readme.md with correctly rewritten relative links, matching root README.md content exactly.

Verified against all 25 real fixtures in data/: 24 still decode HTML body, 1 text-only, 0 errors -- cap doesn't clip legitimate mail.

title: npm test fails out of the box: @vscode/test-electron hardcodes Contents/MacOS/Electron, current VS Code stable ships Contents/MacOS/Code
description: Fresh 'npm test' downloads VS Code 1.136.1 and fails with 'spawn .../Electron ENOENT' (exit -2). node_modules/@vscode/test-electron/out/util.js:184 hardcodes 'Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron' as the executable path for darwin stable, but the downloaded 1.136.1 build only has Contents/MacOS/Code -- the library's assumption is stale for current VS Code releases. Confirmed working around it via VSCODE_TEST_EXECUTABLE_PATH=<path to Contents/MacOS/Code> node out/test/runTest.js (the escape hatch already in src/test/runTest.ts, kept 'optional' by docs/plans/fix_test_electron_wiring.md). Not fixed in repo: default 'npm test' still breaks for anyone without that env var set manually.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) an upstream @vscode/test-electron version fixes the hardcoded path and package.json is bumped, or (b) runTest.ts auto-detects Code vs Electron binary name and sets VSCODE_TEST_EXECUTABLE_PATH itself, or (c) CI/docs pin a known-working VS Code version via a version manifest so the mismatch can't recur silently. Plain 'npm test' from a clean .vscode-test/ must exit 0.
close_reason: Bumped @vscode/test-electron 3.0.0 -> ^3.1.0 in extension/package.json. 3.1.0 resolves the stable-channel executable name from Info.plist/sole-regular-file-in-Contents-MacOS instead of hardcoding 'Electron'. Verified: npm test now exits 0 with all 10 tests passing, no VSCODE_TEST_EXECUTABLE_PATH override needed. npm run lint and npm run package also verified green. No new vulnerabilities (still 6 pre-existing, all devDependency-tree, unrelated). docs/plans/fix_test_electron_wiring.md updated with an addendum documenting this second fix.

title: Dead 'unsupported' code path + stale .eml message, left over from before eml-parsing shipped
description: Noticed while reading emailPreviewProvider.ts for the forward-chain-collapsing change. parsers/index.ts's parseEmailFile() no longer returns {status:'unsupported'} anywhere (both .msg and .eml branches now always resolve to 'ok' or 'error') -- that was the pre-eml-parsing placeholder path. But ParseResult's type union, EmailDocument's unsupported flag, EmailPreviewProvider's handling, and webview/main.ts's renderUnsupported() (which still says '.eml files are not supported yet -- .msg support is implemented first') are all still there, now unreachable. Not urgent -- just dead code + a stale message that would never actually show, since nothing produces status:'unsupported' anymore.
acceptance_criteria: Either remove the unsupported status/branch entirely (parseEmailFile only ever returns ok/error now), or decide there's a genuine future use for it and update renderUnsupported()'s message to not reference .eml specifically.
notes: 2026-09-06: Confirmed still accurate -- re-verified by reading parsers/index.ts, emailPreviewProvider.ts, and webview/main.ts directly; parseEmailFile() only ever returns 'ok'/'error', 'unsupported' is genuinely unreachable in current source. Red herring encountered: user saw the exact '.eml files are not supported yet' message in real VS Code (not the dev host) when opening data/fixtures/nested.eml. Root cause was NOT this dead code path -- it was two separate installed extensions: the stale mailpeek.mailpeek-0.0.1 (installed pre-eml-parsing, whose bundled parsers/index.js hard-returns {status:'unsupported'} for .eml) alongside the current nullgradlabs.mailpeek-0.0.1 (rebuilt/reinstalled this session). Both register the identical customEditors viewType 'mailpeek.emailViewer' with priority:'default' for *.msg/*.eml, and VS Code resolved the conflict in favor of the old one. Cause: publisher field in package.json changed from 'mailpeek' to 'nullgradlabs' (commit 4b43e26), which changes the extension's identity to VS Code's installer, so 'code --install-extension --force' created a second install instead of upgrading the first. Fixed by 'code --uninstall-extension mailpeek.mailpeek'. Lesson for future sessions: if the stale-unsupported-message symptom reappears, check 'code --list-extensions --show-versions | grep mailpeek' for duplicate publisher ids BEFORE assuming this bug's dead code path came back to life.
close_reason: Removed the dead code entirely rather than just leaving it: parsers/index.ts's ParseResult union dropped '{status: unsupported}'; EmailDocument's 'unsupported' constructor param removed; emailPreviewProvider.ts's dead branch and postMessage field removed; webview/main.ts's InitMessage.unsupported field, renderUnsupported() (with the message that referenced the now-deleted docs/plans/initial_plan.md), and its dispatch branch all removed. Verified: npm run compile/test/lint all green (22/22 tests).
